title: LETTER 15: Letter to Bank Manager — Complaint About Mis-selling of Insurance

blocks.content: Topic: Write a letter to the Branch Manager complaining about the mis-selling of an insurance product disguised as a fixed deposit by a bank employee.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Mis-selling of insurance occurs when bank staff bundle investment policies with loans or falsely pitch ULIPs/endowment plans as fixed deposits.
The complaint letter should explicitly state key details: Account Number, Policy Number, Date of Transaction, and the name of the bank representative involved.
Cite the official 'Free-Look Period' rule mandated by IRDAI to demand a full refund without exit penalties.
Maintain a professional, firm tone clearly requesting policy cancellation, full premium credit, and escalation to the Banking Ombudsman if unaddressed.

blocks.content: I request you to look into this matter urgently, process the cancellation of the fraudulently issued policy under the free-look provision, and refund the debited amount to my account.
Subject: Formal Complaint Regarding Mis-selling of Life Insurance Policy as Fixed Deposit — Policy No. LI-2024-456789

I am Meena Krishnan, a senior citizen aged 67, and a pensioner account holder with your branch since 2007 (Account No. INDB-TN-99XXXX). I write to register a serious complaint about what I believe constitutes deliberate mis-selling of a financial product by one of your branch employees.

rows: Market-linked or contingent on policy terms
Premature withdrawal allowed with minor penalty
Heavy surrender charges if lapsed early

blocks.content: On 15 October 2024, I visited your branch intending to renew my Rs. 5,00,000 Fixed Deposit that was maturing. A relationship executive named Mr. Vishal spoke with me and represented a product as a 'special fixed deposit with higher returns' that I should sign up for. Relying on his representations and my long-standing trust in this branch, I signed several documents and authorised a debit of Rs. 5,00,000 from my savings account.

It was only in February 2025, when I inquired about the interest credit on my 'fixed deposit,' that I discovered I had been enrolled in a life insurance ULIP policy with a 10-year lock-in period, with the first year premium of Rs. 5,00,000 already invested. I am a 67-year-old pensioner with no need for a 10-year investment horizon, and this product is entirely unsuitable for my financial profile and circumstances.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and RBI's fair practices guidelines strictly prohibit the mis-selling of insurance products by bank employees under the bancassurance model. I invoke the 30-day free-look period (which I was not informed about) and request: (i) immediate cancellation of the policy and refund of my Rs. 5,00,000 to my savings account; (ii) a written explanation of how this policy was sold without proper disclosures; and (iii) appropriate disciplinary action against the employee concerned.
If this matter is not resolved within 15 days, I intend to escalate it to the RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme and IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal.

items: Letter writing on banking grievances (like mis-selling, unauthorized deductions, or failed ATM transactions) is a high-frequency topic in IBPS PO and SBI PO Mains exams.
Strictly adhere to formal letter conventions: Sender's Address, Date, Receiver's Designation/Address, Concise Subject Line, Formal Salutation, and Sign-off.
Focus on factual clarity, mention specific regulatory timelines (Free-Look Period), and avoid aggressive or informal language.

blocks.content: Examiner's Tip: This letter demonstrates knowledge of bancassurance regulations, IRDAI's free-look period, and customer protection frameworks. Mentioning escalation to the Ombudsman and IRDAI adds legal weight. Senior citizen vulnerability is a common exam theme.
